findings.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner in addGuests.handler.ts is computed with && (isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner), requiring the user to be both admin and owner, so team admins who are not the owner get FORBIDDEN on team bookings

Guest email uniqueness is enforced only client-side in AddGuestsDialog's .refine; the server schema is a bare z.array(z.string().email()) and uniqueGuests only filters emails matching existing attendees without deduping within the input array, with no DB constraint or transaction, allowing duplicate Attendee rows and double-sent booking emails

The blacklisted guest email list is lowercased but compared against raw, non-normalized input (!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)), so addresses like User@BlockedDomain.com bypass the blacklist entirely
BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is read ad hoc via process.env and never registered in the env schema

The booking fetch uses where: { id: bookingId } with no downstream check of booking.status or timing, and the UI adds the menu item unconditionally, allowing guests, calendar updates, and booking emails to be attached to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or past bookings

The permission gate grants add-rights to any attendee of the booking (booking.attendees.find matching user.email) rather than only the organizer or team admin, letting anyone who ever booked a slot attach arbitrary email addresses and trigger organizer-addressed notification emails

Emails already present as attendees are silently dropped from uniqueGuests (mixed input returns success 'Guests added' while discarding them), the all-duplicates case throws the misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid error, and the dialog never displays current guests with no view or remove capability anywhere in the PR

sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input array instead of uniqueGuests, so an email filtered out of the DB write still matches newGuests.includes in email-manager.ts and is re-sent a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added notice

The constructed evt never sets team, yet email-manager.ts branches on calendarEvent.team?.members to notify team members, making the team-member notification loop unreachable dead code so co-hosts of collective/round-robin bookings are never notified

A new generic MultiEmail component is added to the shared packages/ui public export surface for a single consumer, carrying readOnly and placeholder props that AddGuestsDialog never exercises, plus a copy-pasted false comment claiming it is 40kb not every user needs

Authorization predicate in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses `&&` instead of `||` for `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, requiring the caller to be both team admin AND team owner, so a team admin who is not an owner is wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN and the effective access set diverges from the intended 'admin or owner' check

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check in addGuests.handler.ts:70-78 can be bypassed via letter case: the env blacklist is normalized with toLowerCase() but the guest string is compared raw, so submitting 'Attacker@Evil.com' slips past a blacklist entry 'attacker@evil.com', defeating the only server-side control on which addresses receive booking emails
Dedup check `guest === attendee.email` (addGuests.handler.ts:76) is missing email case normalization, so duplicate guests differing only in letter case will not be caught

Unbounded `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts:5 (z.array with no .max()) combined with no rate limiting lets any caller passing the authz gate — including external booking attendees and guests added by this very endpoint — submit thousands of emails per request, causing unbounded BookingAttendee row creation and mass email dispatch (spam relay / DoS primitive)

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a direct read of `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but whether it is “never registered in the env schema” cannot be verified from this diff because no env-schema/validation files are shown or modified here. This claim depends on code/config outside the diff, so it’s not a strictly verifiable defect from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The booking fetch uses where: { id: bookingId } with no downstream check of booking.status or timing, and the UI adds the menu item unconditionally, allowing guests, calendar updates, and booking emails to be attached to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or past bookings

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking with `where: { id: bookingId }` and proceeds to update attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and send emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails`) without any checks on booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or whether the event is in the past. In `BookingListItem`, the new menu action `additional_guests` is added unconditionally to `actions`, so the UI exposes it regardless of booking status/timing. This makes it possible to attach guests/trigger calendar updates/emails for bookings that likely should be immutable (cancelled/rejected/past).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The permission gate grants add-rights to any attendee of the booking (booking.attendees.find matching user.email) rather than only the organizer or team admin, letting anyone who ever booked a slot attach arbitrary email addresses and trigger organizer-addressed notification emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the gate is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`. So a user who is merely an attendee (not organizer/admin) can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests`, which updates booking attendees and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (sending organizer/team-facing notifications as well). This matches the finding that attendees can attach arbitrary emails and trigger notification emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Emails already present as attendees are silently dropped from uniqueGuests (mixed input returns success 'Guests added' while discarding them), the all-duplicates case throws the misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid error, and the dialog never displays current guests with no view or remove capability anywhere in the PR

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). If the input contains a mix of already-attending emails plus at least one new email, the mutation proceeds and returns success while silently ignoring the already-attending emails. If *all* submitted emails are already attendees (or blacklisted), it throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading because the emails may be valid/unique but simply already invited/blocked (schema already enforces email format). On the UI side, AddGuestsDialog only renders a `MultiEmail` input for new entries and does not fetch/display current guests nor provide removal, and BookingListItem only passes `bookingId`, so there is no way in this PR to view/remove existing guests from the dialog.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The constructed evt never sets team, yet email-manager.ts branches on calendarEvent.team?.members to notify team members, making the team-member notification loop unreachable dead code so co-hosts of collective/round-robin bookings are never notified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `evt: CalendarEvent` object passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` does not include any `team` field (only `organizer`, `attendees`, etc.). In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` calls `formatCalEvent(calEvent)` and then conditionally notifies team members only if `calendarEvent.team?.members` exists. Given `evt` never sets `team`, this team-member notification loop will not run for add-guests emails, so additional team/co-host recipients won’t be emailed via that path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A new generic MultiEmail component is added to the shared packages/ui public export surface for a single consumer, carrying readOnly and placeholder props that AddGuestsDialog never exercises, plus a copy-pasted false comment claiming it is 40kb not every user needs

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new `MultiEmail` component under `packages/ui` and exports it from `packages/ui/index.tsx`, and `AddGuestsDialog` is the only shown consumer. However, the proposed finding is primarily about API/maintainability (export surface size, “single consumer”, and having props not currently used by that consumer) rather than a verifiable correctness/bug/security defect introduced by the change. Also, the claim that the “40kb” comment is false is not verifiable from this diff alone, and `readOnly` is in fact exercised by `AddGuestsDialog` (it passes `readOnly={false}`), so that part is misstated. Unused optional props (`placeholder`) are not inherently a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization predicate in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses `&&` instead of `||` for `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, requiring the caller to be both team admin AND team owner, so a team admin who is not an owner is wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN and the effective access set diverges from the intended 'admin or owner' check

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both an admin and an owner. Given the variable name and common authorization intent (“admin OR owner”), this will incorrectly deny access to team admins who are not owners (and vice versa), causing the subsequent `FORBIDDEN` check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`) to reject legitimate users. This is directly verifiable from the diff at the shown lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check in addGuests.handler.ts:70-78 can be bypassed via letter case: the env blacklist is normalized with toLowerCase() but the guest string is compared raw, so submitting 'Attacker@Evil.com' slips past a blacklist entry 'attacker@evil.com', defeating the only server-side control on which addresses receive booking emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the blacklist is built as lowercase strings (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter compares using the raw `guest` value: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not normalized (and the Zod schema `z.string().email()` does not force lowercase), an input like `Attacker@Evil.com` will not match a blacklist entry `attacker@evil.com`, allowing a case-variant to bypass the blacklist check. The same case-sensitive comparison is also used for existing attendee deduplication (`guest === attendee.email`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedup check `guest === attendee.email` (addGuests.handler.ts:76) is missing email case normalization, so duplicate guests differing only in letter case will not be caught

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out existing attendees using a strict case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. The input schema only enforces `z.string().email()` (no lowercasing/normalization), and the client-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog also uses `new Set(emails)` (case-sensitive). Therefore `Foo@bar.com` and `foo@bar.com` will be treated as distinct and can be added as duplicates relative to existing attendees or within the new list, which is a real correctness issue introduced/left unhandled by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts:5 (z.array with no .max()) combined with no rate limiting lets any caller passing the authz gate — including external booking attendees and guests added by this very endpoint — submit thousands of emails per request, causing unbounded BookingAttendee row creation and mass email dispatch (spam relay / DoS primitive)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `addGuests` with input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no `.max()`), and the handler uses the provided list to (1) `createMany` booking attendee rows (`guestsFullDetails` is derived directly from `uniqueGuests`, which is only filtered against existing attendees/blacklist, not size), and (2) trigger email fan-out via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (which iterates over all attendees and sends emails). There is no per-request cap in the schema or handler, so a caller who passes the authz check (`isAttendee` or organizer) can submit an extremely large array and cause large DB writes and mass email dispatch. The mention of “no rate limiting” is not directly verifiable from the diff, but the unbounded per-request amplification primitive is clearly present in the added code.
